newsitem.title: USA: 'Rosie the Riveter' of WW2 movie fame dies.
newsitem.headline: 'Rosie the Riveter' of WW2 movie fame dies.

text.p: Rose Will Monroe, who played "Rosie the Riveter" in a Second World War patriotic movie, died at her home on Saturday. She was 77.
Like thousands of other women during the war, Monroe worked at an aircraft manufacturing plant as part of the United States' war effort.

It was while working at the Willow Run Aircraft Factory in Ypsilanti, Michigan, that a visiting movie company selected Monroe to play the lead role in the short but widely distributed promotional film.
Thereafter, the name "Rosie the Riveter" -- based on a song of the same name -- was widely used as a nickname for women helping the war effort in the nation's plants.
Monroe's daughter, Vickie Jarvis, told the Louisville, Ky., Courier-Journal that her mother had been selected to play the part because she fit the profile of the song.

Unlike many women who returned to the home after the war was won, Monroe remained a member of the work force, handling such jobs as taxi driver and beauty shop owner before starting her own construction company specialising in high-quality custom houses.
Monroe later became a pilot, flying regularly until a 1978 accident destroyed one of her kidneys and the vision in her left eye, Jarvis said.
